M01.reason: Opcode check inverted: a correct AccessAck/AckData response gives PSLVERR=1 and PRDATA=0, and a wrong opcode is not flagged.

M02.reason: Setup is detected in non-IDLE states instead of IDLE, so a legal Setup never launches a request or completes a local error.

M03.reason: REQ leaves on a_ready=0 instead of 1, so channel A drops before acceptance and is held after the handshake.

M04.reason: The WAIT term is inverted: a response in WAIT is not counted, so the transfer hangs, and orphan d_valid in IDLE is counted.

M05.reason: A counted response no longer raises PREADY, so the APB transfer never completes.

M06.reason: PREADY resets to 1 instead of 0, so it is high while reset is asserted.

M07.reason: d_ready is driven to 0 after reset release instead of staying 1, so it never goes high and responses are not accepted.

M08.reason: Local-error branch is inverted: an illegal Setup gets no PREADY/PSLVERR, and other cycles get a spurious local error.

M09.reason: a_valid resets to 1, so o_tlul_a_valid is high during reset.

M10.reason: Source check inverted: a correct d_source gives PSLVERR and a wrong source is accepted as good.

M11.reason: Alignment test is inverted: aligned accesses are treated as illegal and misaligned ones launch a TL-UL request.

M12.reason: In REQ with a_ready the next state is inverted: a same-cycle response goes to WAIT (and then never arrives), and no response sends it to IDLE.

M13.reason: The load is qualified by a non-IDLE state, so a launch in IDLE never loads or starts a request.

M14.reason: A local error no longer raises PREADY, so the illegal transfer does not complete in the first Access cycle.

M15.reason: The default PSLVERR next value is 1, so PSLVERR is high without PREADY and on good completions.

M16.reason: The local-error test in the IDLE branch is inverted: the FSM goes to DONE on a non-Setup idle cycle (blocking the next Setup), and an illegal Setup stays in IDLE.

M17.reason: reg_a_rd resets to 1, so o_tlul_a_opcode is 3'b100 in reset instead of 0.

M18.reason: The response completion is qualified by a non-BUSY state, so a response in BUSY gives no PREADY, and a response in other states gives a spurious one.

M19.reason: Request payload (opcode, address, data) loads when there is no launch instead of on it, so channel A carries wrong or stale values.

M20.reason: a_valid next value is inverted: it is low when a request is presented and high when idle.

M21.reason: A local error completes with PSLVERR=0 instead of 1.

M22.reason: The default PREADY next value is 1, so PREADY is high on every cycle without a completion.

M23.reason: APB FSM reset polarity is inverted: the FSM is held in IDLE while running and takes the next state while in reset, so transfers are not processed and reset does not clear state.

M24.reason: d_ready resets to 1, so o_tlul_d_ready is high during reset.

M25.reason: The strobe test is inverted: full-strobe writes are rejected and partial-strobe writes launch a request.

M26.reason: In WAIT the response branch is inverted: the FSM returns to IDLE with no response, and stays in WAIT after the response.

M27.reason: The REQ-state term is inverted: a same-cycle response during acceptance is not counted, and a response outside REQ is counted.

M28.reason: PSLVERR resets to 1, so it is high without PREADY during reset.

M29.reason: Completion-register reset polarity is inverted: outputs are not cleared in reset and are held at 0 while running, so no completion appears.

M30.reason: TL-UL FSM reset polarity is inverted: it is held in IDLE during normal operation, so no request is ever presented, and reset does not clear it.

M31.reason: The completion condition is negated, so a normal response gives no completion and PREADY/PSLVERR/PRDATA are loaded with garbage on other cycles.

M32.reason: The IDLE branch moves to REQ when there is no launch instead of on a launch, so spurious requests start and legal ones do not.

M33.reason: The APB IDLE branch goes to BUSY when there is no launch instead of on a legal launch, so legal transfers stay in IDLE and idle cycles enter BUSY.

M34.reason: Reset polarity of a_valid/d_ready is inverted: they are cleared while running and set in reset, so there is no request and d_ready is 0 in operation.

M35.reason: BUSY goes to DONE when there is no response instead of on one, so the APB FSM leaves BUSY early and misses the real completion.

M36.reason: Payload-register reset polarity is inverted: opcode, address and data are not cleared in reset and are held at 0 while running, so requests have wrong content.
